label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: Let $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$ and satisfy $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; 0\; x$ for all $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$. Then $G(x) = G(a)$ for all $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$.
proof: Let $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$. If $x = a$ the result is immediate. Otherwise $a < x$, so we restrict $G$ to $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; x$ (which inherits continuity) and note the derivative hypothesis restricts to $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; x$. By the Mean Value Theorem (\texttt{exists\_hasDerivAt\_eq\_slope}), there exists $c \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; x$ with $G'(c) = (G(x) - G(a))/(x - a)$. Since $G'(c) = 0$ by hypothesis and $x - a \neq 0$, we conclude $G(x) = G(a)$.
